samples.title: Booking rack: Proof strip
samples.statement:
Inputs
`drawers` is a list of bookings. Each row is [start, end].

Your tasks
1. Create a list `acceptedLengths`. Each booking is [start, end]. It uses time from start up to, but not including, end. Sort bookings by end time, from earliest to latest. For matching end times, put the earlier start first. Accept the first booking. Then accept a booking only if it starts at or after the end of the last one accepted. Record the length, end - start, of each accepted booking. Keep acceptance order. Negative times are allowed. With no bookings, `acceptedLengths` is empty.
2. Complete `bookingRackProofStrip` so it returns `acceptedLengths`. Return it, do not print it.

Example
If `drawers` is [[3, 7], [9, 11], [14, 20], [6, 10], [0, 5]], then `acceptedLengths` is [5, 4, 6] and `bookingRackProofStrip` returns [5, 4, 6].

Rules
- If `acceptedLengths` is empty, return [].

Test data
TEST DATA 1: `drawers` is [[7, 8], [8, 9], [2, 3], [17, 18], [-8, -2]].
TEST DATA 2: `drawers` is [[3, 7], [0, 2], [5, 9], [6, 10]].

samples.title: Booking rack: Floor ticket
samples.statement:
Inputs
`drawers` is a list of bookings. Each row is [start, end].

Your tasks
1. Create a list `acceptedLengths`. Each booking is [start, end]. It uses time from start up to, but not including, end. Sort bookings by end time, from earliest to latest. For matching end times, put the earlier start first. Accept the first booking. Then accept a booking only if it starts at or after the end of the last one accepted. Record the length, end - start, of each accepted booking. Keep acceptance order. Negative times are allowed. With no bookings, `acceptedLengths` is empty.
2. Find the smallest number in `acceptedLengths`. Store it in `smallest`.
3. Complete `bookingRackFloorTicket` so it returns `smallest`. Return it, do not print it.

Example
If `drawers` is [[1, 3], [-7, -5], [7, 13], [6, 10], [7, 11]], then `acceptedLengths` is [2, 2, 4] and `bookingRackFloorTicket` returns 2.

Rules
- If `acceptedLengths` is empty, return 0.

Test data
TEST DATA 1: `drawers` is [[0, 1], [16, 18], [14, 20], [15, 21], [-4, -2]].
TEST DATA 2: `drawers` is [[3, 7], [-8, -5], [5, 9], [6, 10]].

samples.title: Booking rack: Boss receipt
samples.statement:
Inputs
`drawers` is a list of bookings. Each row is [start, end].

Your tasks
1. Create a list `acceptedLengths`. Each booking is [start, end]. It uses time from start up to, but not including, end. Sort bookings by end time, from earliest to latest. For matching end times, put the earlier start first. Accept the first booking. Then accept a booking only if it starts at or after the end of the last one accepted. Record the length, end - start, of each accepted booking. Keep acceptance order. Negative times are allowed. With no bookings, `acceptedLengths` is empty.
2. Multiply each number in `acceptedLengths` by its position, counting from 1: the first number by 1, the second by 2, and so on.
3. Add those products. Store the sum in `weightedTotal`.
4. Complete `bookingRackBossReceipt` so it returns `weightedTotal`. Return it, do not print it.

Example
If `drawers` is [[5, 11], [9, 11], [9, 10], [8, 14], [-3, -2]], then `acceptedLengths` is [1, 1] and `bookingRackBossReceipt` returns 3.

Rules
- If `acceptedLengths` is empty, return 0.

Test data
TEST DATA 1: `drawers` is [[15, 17], [1, 2], [19, 23], [-4, -3], [21, 25]].
TEST DATA 2: `drawers` is [[9, 12], [10, 13], [-5, -4], [12, 15]].
